# Two Surfaces of Ambiguity: Complementary Detection for Text-to-SQL

## Research question

Question-only introspection and candidate-SQL disagreement may expose different underspecified choices, but broader detection need not improve the answer delivered under a clarification budget.

## Method

Compares single and sampled introspection with single-pass and independently sampled SQL candidates. SQL methods analyze structural differences to generate clarification questions; a union combines the channels. Detection uses a cross-model simulator encoder, while a separate agent receives a question pool and chooses interactions.

## Evaluation

BIRD-Interact-Lite supplies 300 tasks and 1,550 annotated terms across 18 databases. Four models are tested for detection; three open-weight models for agentic stress-mode evaluation. Most stochastic open-model detector runs use three seeds; deterministic introspection and proprietary-model results use one. AMBROSIA transfer covers 1,149 ambiguous questions with Qwen3.5-122B.

## What the results support

Union recall exceeds either low-budget detector, with different subtype strengths. Both introspection and union improve over the ReAct baseline, but their downstream differences are not significant. On AMBROSIA, AllFound rises from 2.5% to 13.4% while precision falls from 45.2% to 20.9% and average unique SQLs rise from 2.0 to 6.9. Multi-label scoring changes masked-knowledge recall without establishing better user interaction.

## Limits and qualifications

All interactive evidence uses simulated users and benchmark annotations. The union emits more questions and SQL candidates; its three-call count excludes encoder calls and the subsequent agent loop. Rare subtypes have few examples. Structural diversity does not prove semantic alternatives, and no user-budget-aware ranking method is evaluated. Ground-truth dependencies and a paper/README baseline discrepancy limit reproduction claims.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Direct ambiguity-detection and clarification research that separates detection coverage, annotation/scoring effects, interpretation-set precision and downstream success.
